q-122559.name: Question 1
q-122559.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14121490/assets/cfc15b6202167211b7d6c0e8f6635dd9e571810d5296a209a4c317350604c4a4.png)

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?
q-122559.worked_solution:
We notice the following:

- Each vector in our vector field is parallel to the $x$-axis. So, the $j$ and $k$ components of our vector field are zero everywhere. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
H(x,y,z)=i+j+k,\,
$$

- Moreover, each vector in our vector field is pointing in the *positive* $x$-direction, so the $i$ component of our vector field is positive. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
G(x,y,z)=-i
$$

- Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the $i$ component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
K(x,y,z)={e}^{x}\,i
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field $F(x,y,z)=i.$

q-122559.html:
Question 1
?

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?

a
F(x,y,z)=i
b
H(x,y,z)=i+j+k
c
None of the listed
d
K(x,y,z)=exi
e
G(x,y,z)=−i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We notice the following:

  • Each vector in our vector field is parallel to the x-axis. So, the j and k components of our vector field are zero everywhere. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: H(x,y,z)=i+j+k,

  • Moreover, each vector in our vector field is pointing in the positive x-direction, so the i component of our vector field is positive. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: G(x,y,z)=−i

  • Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the i component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: K(x,y,z)=exi

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field F(x,y,z)=i.

q-122632.name: Question 2
q-122632.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14121490/assets/a032eb49f78ce7bd54de6969f030e4316f2bd3028280f73991af3fe45521733c.png)

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?
q-122632.worked_solution:
We notice the following:

- The horizontal component (i.e., the $i$ component) is zero for *every* vector in our vector field. Therefore, we can rule out the following options:

$$
F(x,y)=i+j,\,K(x,y)=-i-2\,j
$$

- As we move away from the origin in the horizontal direction, our vectors' vertical components (i.e., the $j$ components) get longer. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
G(x,y)=5\,j
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field $H(x,y)=x\,j.$

b
F(x,y)=i+j
c
G(x,y)=5j
d
H(x,y)=xj
e
None of the listed
Submit
Incorrect

We notice the following:

  • The horizontal component (i.e., the i component) is zero for every vector in our vector field. Therefore, we can rule out the following options: F(x,y)=i+j,K(x,y)=−i−2j

  • As we move away from the origin in the horizontal direction, our vectors' vertical components (i.e., the j components) get longer. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: G(x,y)=5j

q-122670.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14121490/assets/64f02fa7dcd23b20e61801c0453d8fe7ed013936572e1ee63f748361edd4dec5.png)

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?
q-122670.worked_solution:
We notice the following:

- Each vector in our vector field is parallel to the $z$-axis. So, the $i$ and $j$ components of our vector field are zero everywhere. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
F(x,y,z)=i,\,G(x,y,z)=-j
$$

- Moreover, each vector in our vector field is pointing in the *negative* $z$-direction, so the $k$ component of our vector field is negative. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
H(x,y,z)=k
$$

- Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the $k$ component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
K(x,y,z)=-{x}^{2}\,k
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram doesn't correspond to any of the listed vector fields.

Question 3
?

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?

a
G(x,y,z)=−j
b
None of the listed
c
K(x,y,z)=−x2k
d
F(x,y,z)=i
e
H(x,y,z)=k
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We notice the following:

  • Each vector in our vector field is parallel to the z-axis. So, the i and j components of our vector field are zero everywhere. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: F(x,y,z)=i,G(x,y,z)=−j

  • Moreover, each vector in our vector field is pointing in the negative z-direction, so the k component of our vector field is negative. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: H(x,y,z)=k

  • Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the k component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option: K(x,y,z)=−x2k

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram doesn't correspond to any of the listed vector fields.

q-122758.name: Question 4
q-122758.problem: Which of the following diagrams represents the vector field $F(x,y)=-x\,i-y\,j$ at the indicated points?
q-122758.worked_solution:
We have to sketch the vector field at the points $(1,4),(2,-2),$ and $(4,-2).$

To sketch the vector field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the function $F(x,y)=-x\,i-y\,j\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1,4) & =-(1)\,i-4\,j=-i-4\,j \\ F(2,-2) & =-(2)\,i-(-2)\,j=-2\,i+2\,j \\ F(4,-2) & =-(4)\,i-(-2)\,j=-4\,i+2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

We now draw our vectors. At each point, we draw the vector associated with that point, placing the tail end of the vector on the point itself. This gives the following diagram.

q-123748.name: Question 5
q-123748.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14121490/assets/bff60466ca8abba4fd849c046c02af3a4811279774975fc981cafad91d734ed5.png)

Which of the following could be the function that generates the vector field above?
q-123748.worked_solution:
We notice the following:

- Each vector in our vector field is parallel to the $x$-axis. So, the $j$ and $k$ components of our vector field are zero everywhere. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
K(x,y,z)=-i+j
$$

- Moreover, each vector in our vector field is pointing in the *negative* $x$-direction, so the $i$ component of our vector field is negative. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
F(x,y,z)=i
$$

- Finally, we note that each vector in our vector field has the same length, so the $i$ component of our vector field is constant. Therefore, we can rule out the following option:

$$
G(x,y,z)=-y\,i
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the diagram corresponds to the vector field $H(x,y,z)=-2\,i.$
